clue.text: Fixed fee to cover account after potential turnaround

indicators.note: the rearranged fee with its contents comes after the unit of potential

parts.note: the volt is the unit of electrical potential

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, as a lid covers what is beneath
something fixed has been adjusted or rigged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fixed charge is changed to cover an account after some possible reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' reads as possible, but it is the electrical unit; 'Fixed' rearranges FEE to EFE before 'to cover' wraps it round the account letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, a borrowing from French and Italian.

clue.text: See later deposit slips after five

indicators.note: the shuffled deposit follows the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the letters of the word deposit slip out of place, forming a new order

explanation.surface: A bank instruction: look at the paying-in slips filed after the fifth one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit slips' reads as paying-in forms, but 'slips' is the anagram signal, its result IDEPOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Vide post is a Latin reference note in books meaning look at what comes further on.

clue.text: Blair kept box in which even letters deceive

indicators.note: only the second, fourth and so on letters of each of the three words are kept

explanation.surface: A dig at Tony Blair: the box he kept held letters meant to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are taken word by word: LI from Blair, ET from kept, O from box.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie to someone is to mislead them with falsehoods, the verb phrase matching deceive.

clue.text: So there is a leak, perhaps from gorges

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the phrase so there is a leak is just one possible ordering of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone spots dripping water coming from ravines in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorges' looks like a plural noun for ravines, but it is the verb meaning stuffs oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gorges eats enormous quantities, which the idiom compares to a hungry farm animal.

clue.text: Little old man of legend in an appellation

indicators.note: the folklore figure sits within the two letters of the little word an

parts.note: a gnome is a small bearded figure of folklore

explanation.surface: A folk tale's little old man is known by some formal name.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnomen is an extra name or epithet, like a nickname added in Roman naming, so a kind of appellation.

clue.text: What about slingshot for breakfast?

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the other piece

parts.note: eh? is a request to repeat something, like what?

indicators.note: shot as in shot to pieces, so the letters of sling are broken up

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is a catapult really what one eats in the morning?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slingshot' must be split, with 'shot' the anagram signal on its first part. A full English is a British cooked breakfast of eggs, bacon and sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: In British cafés an English, as in a full English, is the cooked morning meal of fried foods.

clue.text: Old and heartless, OK!

indicators.note: the middle of the word is cut out, leaving its outer parts

parts.note: OK! as an answer means agreed

explanation.surface: Someone accepts, with a cheerful OK, being called old and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes RE, the two middle letters of AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is a plain synonym for elderly, describing a person well on in years.

clue.text: Brainwave said in response to "what goes with a grey suit, darling?"

indicators.note: the reply is spoken, so it is its sound that counts

parts.words: what goes with a grey suit, darling
parts.note: a grey tie, dear, would match such a suit

explanation.surface: Someone asks their partner for help choosing an accessory for a grey suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken answer 'grey tie, dear' runs together into the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, the sort greeted with enthusiastic approval.

clue.text: Dislike taking part in aptitude testing

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to sit an aptitude test.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, a stronger form of the verb to dislike.

clue.text: The sexes in science recur, after setting boundaries

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes inside the rearranged words
the words science recur are set in a new arrangement

parts.note: male and female, abbreviated M and F

explanation.surface: A remark that gender keeps cropping up in science once limits are laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After setting' rearranges SCIENCE RECUR to CIRCUERENCES, and 'in' puts MF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A circumference is the boundary line of a circle or round area, so plural perimeters.

clue.text: Lived in Germany with the world of the Germans

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
Welt is German for world

explanation.surface: Someone lived in Germany and absorbed the German view of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, an old-fashioned way of saying resided.

clue.text: Slack peignoir (night clothing)

parts.note: a peignoir is a light dressing gown, also called a negligee or négligé

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word night are its clothing, wrapped around the rest

explanation.surface: A loose dressing gown worn as night clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'night clothing' look like a gloss on the gown, but it yields only NT, the outside of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack here means careless or lax, describing someone who fails to take proper care.

clue.text: Difficulty with Mao parable, but not as translated

indicators.note: a translation changes the form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letters named next are taken away

parts.note: As read as the plural of the letter A, so every A is meant

explanation.surface: Rendering one of Chairman Mao's parables into another language proves tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' means all the letter As: removing the three in MAO PARABLE leaves MOPRBLE, which 'translated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a matter that is hard to deal with, a direct synonym for a difficulty.

clue.text: Provokes auditory perceptions in certain places

indicators.note: what the ear perceives, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: in sites, in particular spots or locations

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble by what people hear in particular locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perceptions' tempts towards INSIGHTS, but the heard words are 'in sites'.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir someone up or urge them on, so it matches provokes.

clue.text: Fogey briefly holding these people under detention to begin with

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: holding fast, as glue keeps things sticking
them refers to a group of people

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the words under and detention are used

explanation.surface: An old fogey briefly kept a group of people locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the final G of STICKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe a dull old-fashioned person resistant to change.

clue.text: Popular star to right of pioneer

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A well-loved celebrity stands to the right of a trailblazer in a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator introduces new ideas or methods, just as a pioneer opens a new field.

clue.text: Insurance on Harley-Davidson — a vanishing breed

parts.note: a hedge is a safeguard against loss, as in hedging bets
hog is slang for a Harley-Davidson motorcycle

explanation.surface: Insurance cover on a classic motorbike, an increasingly rare type of machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breed' suggests a dying sort of biker, but it means an animal kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny mammal of gardens and hedges is in steep decline in Britain, a species dwindling away.

clue.text: Perhaps she meant to eat at dawn, or similar

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the other piece, as a mouth takes in food
perhaps says she meant is only a possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: dawn is early in the day

explanation.surface: Someone apparently intended to have breakfast at first light, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' turns SHE MEANT into NTHESAME, and 'to eat' puts EARLY inside after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Things almost identical are alike, so the phrase is a looser way of saying similar.

clue.text: Irish leader visiting troubled Ulster gets more passionate

indicators.note: the letter drops in on the jumbled word, staying inside it
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of Ulster are jumbled; it also nods to the Troubles
the leader of the word Irish is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Irish politician touring Northern Ireland during unrest grows more fervent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is Northern Ireland; 'troubled' recalls the Troubles there but scrambles ULSTER to LUSTER, and 'visiting' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and full of desire, so the comparative means showing more ardour.

clue.text: Diatribes with no final school qualification turn out the same

definitions.note: refers back to diatribes: the answer means the same thing

indicators.note: turn out suggests the remaining letters are turned into a new order
the qualification's letters are removed from the word

parts.note: IB, the International Baccalaureate, is a diploma taken at the end of school

explanation.surface: Rants by people who failed their final exams all end up sounding alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes IB from DIATRIBES, and 'turn out' rearranges DATRIES; 'the same' means the answer is another word for diatribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, the same thing as a diatribe.

clue.text: Makes sense for tots

definitions.meaning: a story that ... is coherent and believable
to tot is to total a column of figures

explanation.surface: Something is understandable to small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' looks like toddlers, but it is the verb meaning sums.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both is logically consistent and totals figures.

clue.text: Shifty of you French to pinch Naomi's bottom

indicators.note: the French words squeeze the letter between them, catching it inside

parts.note: de vous is French for of you

indicators.note: the bottom of Naomi is the end of her name, its final letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky Frenchman shiftily pinches Naomi's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pinch' places I inside DEVOUS, between the V and the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious describes someone underhand and not to be trusted, the same sense as shifty.

clue.text: Slippery one in band is staggering

indicators.note: the fish sits within the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A slippery character in a music group is astonishing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a music group but means a ring; 'staggering' looks like amazing but means lurching.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling describes swaying unsteadily on one's feet, as does staggering.

clue.text: Middle Eastern fuel qualifier when refined

indicators.note: refining processes the material into something new, here reworking the letters once fuel is taken out

explanation.surface: Oil from the Middle East must pass a quality check after refining.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of QUALIFIER, less those of FUEL, rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a country of the Middle East, so the adjective describes something from there.

clue.text: Met inquiry into a serious tax evasion fraud Detective Sergeant leads astray

indicators.note: the letters gathered are led off course, scrambled into another order
the leading letters of the nine words from inquiry to Sergeant are taken

parts.words: inquiry into a serious tax evasion fraud Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A police investigation into big tax fraud goes off track because the detective sergeant misleads it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like the Metropolitan Police, London's force, but it is the verb, as in met a need.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a requirement or demand is to fulfil it, so met here means fulfilled or contented.

clue.text: Pound in banknotes and coins producing conflict

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the money

parts.note: notes and coins are cash
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Money in sterling notes and coins causes a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a fight or sharp disagreement, the same as a conflict.

clue.text: Advantage of a copper kettle

indicators.note: of says the answer is part of the following words, running from the end of copper into kettle

explanation.surface: A selling point of an old-fashioned copper kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is a perquisite, a benefit that comes with a job or position.

clue.text: Being uncooperative, is asleep outside

indicators.note: the word for asleep goes around the other piece

parts.note: someone resting may be asleep

explanation.surface: A sleeping person refuses to cooperate, staying put outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' sounds like a place to sleep rough, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Resisting means opposing or refusing to go along with something, being obstructive.
